title: OpenStax uses gooses and mouses as examples of an over-applied plural rule
summary: OpenStax says young children may add a regular plural ending to exceptions, saying forms like gooses or mouses.
body: OpenStax Psychology 7.2 describes overgeneralization as extending a language rule to an exception. In English, a plural is often marked with an s, as in dogs, and the textbook says young children may say gooses or mouses before they learn the exceptions. It treats those mistakes as evidence that the regular rule is understood. The examples are the chapter's, credited in the section to Moskowitz, 1978. They are not errors to copy as standard English, and the book is the CC BY 4.0 first edition.
